TIL TIL Japan's bullet train (Shinkansen) has experienced no accidents resulting in fatalities or injuries to onboard passengers since the system opened in 1964. A perfect safety record.

Living in Japan for a few years now, it's sad how often I opt-out of taking the Shinkansen in favor of a budget flight. The bullet trains are extremely convenient and I only live about 5 minutes away from one of the major stations. That said, they are expensive... You can pay ~100 USD each way and now that budget flights are around, it makes it less and less desirable for those on a tighter budget (Budget flights can be around 40 USD).

There are some funny messages when the Shinkansen is delayed though, out in some of the tracks some animals get in the way. I have seen "Bear Collision" in a delay report before.

Several years ago I visited and took the Shinkansen. Midway through transit they announced that the train will be delayed and were extremely apologetic. The travel time was listed as 2 hours, 35 minutes. The delay was, literally, 2 minutes.

Sounds about right really. A lot of working people on commute have to take the trains and they will sometimes have their timing down to the 10 minute mark. We depend on those schedules a lot and when there's a delay it helps that they report on it so much so you can tell your boss what happened.
Speaking of cabin announcements, I like how the cabin message in the Shinkansen calls it a "Superexpress"...telling you that it's no ordinary train.

I would love to see Bear Collision pop up when I visit Japan next month and ride the hell out of that Shinkansen (JR Pass 14 days because the current itinerary has us going all over Honshu).
